outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms are expected this afternoon and evening across parts of the upper Mississippi Valley and northern Michigan. All severe hazards are possible, including the potential for a strong tornado. A few severe storms are also possible across parts of northwestern Arizona into southern Nevada and southwest Utah tonight.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Strong shortwave trough currently moving into the northern Rockies is expected to continue eastward, moving through the northern Plains and reaching the Upper Midwest Wednesday evening. Surface low associated with this system will move eastward across SD early in the period before then accelerating northeastward into northern Ontario. Strong cold front attendant to the surface low will sweep quickly eastward/southeastward through the northern/central Plains and upper/mid MS Valley. Farther west, the upper low currently centered off the central CA coast will transition to an open wave while becoming more progressive and moving across southern CA. Strong mid-level flow accompanying the system will spread across the Lower CO River Valley and into AZ during the second half of the period.

sections.title: Upper Midwest/Upper Great Lakes into the Central Plains
sections.text: Warm-air advection showers and thunderstorms will likely be ongoing across portions of the upper Great Lakes and northern Upper Midwest at the beginning of the period. These showers and thunderstorms are expected to gradually drift northeastward at the warm front lifts northward. By 18Z, surface low ahead of the approaching shortwave trough will likely be centered over west-central MN with a warm front extending northeastward from the low into north-central WI and then southeastward into central Lower MI. A strong cold front will also extend from this low southwestward across central NE and into western KS. Air mass between these two boundaries will be characterized by dewpoints in the mid to upper 60s. Dewpoints may reach 70 deg F in IA. When coupled with modest daytime heating, this moist low-level air mass will support a moderately to strongly unstable environment during the afternoon and evening. Afternoon thunderstorm initiation is first expected near or just east the surface low across central MN along and north of the warm front. sections.title: Southern NV/Southwest UT/Northwest AZ
sections.text: At least scattered thunderstorm coverage is anticipated across CA and much of the Great Basin as strong forcing for ascent attendant to the progressive upper low interacts with remnant moisture brought into the region by tropical cyclone Rosa. Limited instability should keep any severe threat isolated throughout the day but strengthening mid-level flow attendant to the upper low will result in increased vertical shear during evening and overnight across portions of southern NV, southwest UT, and northwest AZ. As a result, despite unfavorable timing, some of these storms may become organized enough to produce hail and/or strong wind gusts. ..Mosier/Bentley.. 10/03/2018

outlooks.summary: Numerous severe storms are possible, most likely between 1 to 11 PM CDT, across parts of the Upper Midwest and Upper Great Lakes States. An intense tornado or two is possible, particularly across parts of north-central WI, along with destructive wind gusts and large hail.

sections.title: Upper Midwest/Upper Great Lakes
sections.text: Strongly considered an upgrade to Moderate Risk for tornado across a small part of north-central WI and wind across a small part of northeast WI, but have deferred to later outlooks. A compact shortwave trough over northern MT will move east and reach northern MN by evening. Amplification of flow throughout the troposphere is anticipated in the warm sector attendant to a deepening surface cyclone tracking northeast from southwest SD to Lake Superior. A warm front is rapidly advancing north and should reach portions of northern WI and Lower MI by afternoon. The thermal gradient across the boundary will be enhanced by differential heating given ongoing elevated convection/cloud coverage north of it and robust insolation south of it. CAMs are reasonably consistent that initially elevated convection should transition to becoming surface-based during the early afternoon in southeast MN to west-central WI. This may emanate from current elevated convection in northwest IA. Rapid strengthening is anticipated towards mid-afternoon as moderate buoyancy characterized by MLCAPE of 1000-2000 J/kg becomes prevalent across central/southern WI with surface temperatures warming into the middle 70s

sections.title: Eastern IA/northern IL to central KS
sections.text: This evening as a powerful cold front sweeps southeast, scattered storms should develop southwest along the boundary. A pronounced gradient in deep-layer shear is expected near the IA/MO border, suggesting that organized convection is more probable in the IA/IL region. The temporal extent of this threat should be limited by the progressive, undercutting nature of the front along with an increasingly confined corridor of instability ahead of the boundary tonight.

sections.title: Desert Southwest
sections.text: With eastward approach of a shortwave trough off the southern CA coast, isolated to scattered storms should develop this evening into tonight. Upper-level winds will be quite strong, but lower-level winds should remain modest. Given unfavorable timing of stronger forced ascent arriving past the diurnal heating cycle, overall setup does not appear particularly conducive to an appreciable corridor of severe wind and hail. However, setup should favor a broader region of isolated occurrences from both hazards. ..Grams/Smith.. 10/03/2018

sections.title: DISCUSSION
sections.text: A few changes have been made to the outlook for this issuance. The first change to the outlook is to expand the slight risk area westward across most of northwest Wisconsin. A 15 percent probability for hail and wind damage is forecast in this area late this afternoon. The second change to the outlook is to confine the 30 percent probability contour for hail to just north-central Wisconsin where the far western part of the enhanced risk area is located. The threat for supercells with a potential for large hail are expected to be most prevalent in north-central Wisconsin through early this evening. The third change to the outlook is to expand the slight risk and marginal areas southeastward across parts of the southern Great Lakes region where a line of thunderstorms is forecast late this evening. The fourth change to the outlook is to expand the thunder area southward across parts of Oklahoma, northern Arkansas and southern Missouri where new model forecasts suggest that thunderstorms may occur late tonight. ..Broyles.. 10/03/2018 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1135 AM CDT Wed Oct 03 2018/

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms remain likely this evening into a portion of tonight across a portion of the upper Great Lakes. Damaging wind is the primary threat, but a few tornadoes and possibly a strong tornado are also possible, especially over northeast Wisconsin this evening.

sections.title: Upper Great Lakes region
sections.text: VWP data indicate the low-level jet has strengthened to 60+ kt over eastern WI in association with a deepening surface low over southern Ontario responding to a progressive shortwave trough moving through the northern Plains. Numerous discrete storms are developing along the strengthening warm conveyor belt as well as farther west along the cold front over western WI. Most storms in the warm sector have been slow to organize, most likely because they remain slightly elevated above the surface layer. However, at least weak to modest low-level theta-e advection with upper 60s F dewpoints will support updrafts rooted close enough to the surface for a threat of low-level mesocyclones and a few tornadoes, especially given size of 0-1 km hodographs. Otherwise, both linear and embedded supercell structures will remain likely with activity developing farther west along the cold front. The threat for damaging wind and isolated tornadoes will persist into tonight as activity continues east into lower MI within a high shear/low CAPE environment.

sections.title: Middle Mississippi Valley through central Plains
sections.text: A few strong to severe storms remain possible this evening with storms developing along the southeast-advancing cold front within the moderately unstable environment. While wind profiles are much weaker than farther north, supporting multicell storm modes, a few storms could produce locally strong wind gusts and hail. ..Dial.. 10/04/2018

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms should gradually expand/intensify across northern/central Wisconsin late this afternoon into this evening. A few tornadoes, damaging winds, and isolated large hail will be possible. Tornado Watch issuance is expected before 4pm CDT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A somewhat uncertain mesoscale/convective evolution is anticipated this afternoon/evening, given the influence of multiple corridors of forcing for ascent and the predominance of cloud cover from eastern Minnesota to the Michigan Upper Peninsula. Recent 18Z soundings from GRB/MPX show moderate inhibition for surface-based parcels, resulting from limited heating due to the aforementioned cloud cover. However, given the approach of a more substantive shortwave trough from the Dakotas into Minnesota this afternoon, as well as northward advection of a warm/moist low-level air mass, inhibition is expected to decrease sufficiently for surface-based development around 4-6pm CDT. The most likely area for such development seemingly exists across northern Wisconsin into the Michigan UP. Elevated convection currently observed near/east of the Minneapolis area may begin to encounter adequate boundary-layer conditions (characterized by surface temperatures reaching near 70) to become surface based by late afternoon. Very strong low-level shear and MLCAPE upwards of 1000-1500 J/kg may yield a cluster of embedded supercells and localized bowing segments, with an attendant threat of a few tornadoes, damaging winds, and isolated large hail. Greater uncertainty regarding timing of severe convection exists farther south over central Wisconsin. Still, the eventual approach of the cold front should yield at least isolated severe storms by mid evening, and these storms may also produce a couple of tornadoes, damaging winds, and large hail, as cells advance eastward towards Lake Michigan. This gradual increase in the overall severe threat over the region will necessitate a Tornado Watch before 4pm CDT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered severe storms are expected to develop along the cold front, with severe wind gusts and a few tornadoes possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A strong cold front is currently approaching the Twin Cities as of 22Z, and extends southwestward into northwest IA. Widespread clouds have kept temperatures cool from MSP eastward into central WI, and this has created an effective warm front from southeast MN into west-central WI. To the southwest of this area, and ahead of the cold front, the boundary layer has become more mixed, with warmer temperatures and wind gusts to over 30 kt from IA into southern WI. Recently, storms have formed just west of MSP, along the accelerating cold front where lift is strong enough to break the capping inversion. Although low-level winds will veer near the front, shear profiles will remain favorable for supercells with ample low-level SRH and lengthening hodographs aloft. The greatest tornado potential may be with the activity developing over MN which will move into the existing tornado watch 395. Additional development is expected through evening along the front into IA and southern WI. Supercells will be possible, but the strong linear forcing mechanism may result in mixed storm modes, with damaging wind and tornado potential.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered thunderstorms are likely to develop this evening, and a few may become marginally severe with a hail or wind threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible imagery shows TCU developing near a surface trough from southwest KS into northwest MO, ahead of the primary cold front which is rapidly approaching from the north. MLCAPE of up to 2000 J/kg has developed from south central KS into IA, and winds veer with height and may support a few cells capable of hail or locally damaging wind gusts. Storms are first expected to form within the pre-frontal trough where temperatures are hot, and then may increase in coverage further as the cold front interacts with the unstable air mass, especially from northeast KS into northern MO. Any severe threat will be maximized during the first few hours after development, with decreasing intensity during the late evening.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe threat may persist into the evening hours. Main threats would be marginally severe hail/gusty winds. A tornado cannot be ruled out. The need for a downstream WW issuance is not clear at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong storms oriented in a northeast to southwest band, along a cold front, are propagating eastward across portions of eastern Wisconsin, towards a generally more stable airmass. An impressive kinematic environment remains in place, with 0148 UTC GRR WSR-88D VWP data indicating over 500 m2/s2 0-1km SRH and over 800 m2/s2 in the 0-3km layer, with 50+ knots of effective bulk shear values present across much of the discussion area. While a relatively moist surface airmass remains in place across Tornado Watch 0395, with WAA aloft continuing ahead of the cold front, modest mid-level lapse rates (5.5-6.0 C/km) and boundary layer nocturnal cooling across and downstream of the current Watch will counteract the WAA, with only marginal destabilization expected. Given the strong shear in place, any storm that can become organized will have the potential to produce marginally severe hail in addition to damaging wind gusts. Though the tendency will be for storms to become elevated with continued boundary layer stabilization, any storm that can remain discrete and surface based for a longer period of time may acquire at least transient low-level rotation and perhaps produce a tornado, particularly along a warm front located across portions of northern into central Michigan, where locally stronger buoyancy and shear are present. However, given the marginal buoyancy, it is not clear if a downstream WW issuance is needed over portions of lower Michigan.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered storms capable of producing hail are expected to persist for several more hours tonight.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Sporadic thunderstorms over southern CA have likely produced marginally severe hail this evening, in advance of an upper trough that continues to move eastward. Despite the loss of daytime heating, cooling aloft will persist across the region maintaining instability. 00Z soundings show that shear profiles are quite favorable for cellular activity, and the cool midlevel temperatures will support hail production. Cells now approaching the CO river may affects parts of southern NV, with the greatest concentration expected over northwestern AZ tonight where upslope flow will aid storm development.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A narrow corridor of severe wind potential is possible across central Lower Michigan if storms maintain strength off Lake Michigan.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A cluster of storms is currently traversing the central part of Lake Michigan, and shows signs of organization on the mesoscale. Wind profiles remain very strong, and a few severe wind gusts are possible despite relatively weak instability. These storms are expected to be strongest as they reach the eastern shores of the lake, and gradually weaken across central Lower Michigan where instability decreases. Given the expected small area of severe potential and short term threat, a watch is not currently anticipated.
